review.brief: Review tier 3 of RM67 on branch ft/RM67-MAG-73-vehicle-monthly-metrics-table. Read the DIFF of the three commits 3466fad, 48b3c31, 305b2f6 against a6b007b - not the whole module. Validate: (1) module-boundary compliance - analytics reads charging ONLY through its public ports, no internals, no cross-module DB read except the test-fixture DELETEs scoped by tesla_id; (2) every doc-pack convention, especially ai/go-conventions.md; (3) spec and tasks coverage - all 7 tasks in tasks.md are ticked and each is really done; (4) the tests - judge them by READING them, never by running them; (5) compliance with the declared Performance-Profile; (6) that NO database object changed - design.md D7 says this tier needs no migration, no query.sql edit and no new charging port. A schema change here is a blocker finding, because the owner confirmed tier 2's schema and never confirmed a new one; (7) that the three DB-integration tests assert the expected values design.md's Test Contract authored UP FRONT (T-CHG-INT-1/2/3), not values reverse-engineered from the implementation. This is the finding most worth hunting; (8) the anti-gaming checks - no acceptance criterion weakened or deleted, no self-approved status. Also check the B2 code-comment rule on NEW comments only: a new comment must not cite design.md, a decision ID, a change or roadmap ID, a tier number, or a ticket ID. The module has many PRE-EXISTING such citations; those are legacy and out of scope - do not report them. The leader already fixed one new violation in monthly_sync.go. Signals: the ASSISTANT ran go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l internal/analytics, and the guards boundary, tz, delta, money, naming and archive - all clean. The USER ran make test and make test-with-db and reported both passing. The assistant never ran any test suite. Do not run one either.
